events.continuity_hook: This begins the next work-trip planning cycle after the Nashville certification travel is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked plan for arrival day, flight routing, rental-car need, hotel area, recovery amenities, parking, and the schedule questions Erin should confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After Nashville, Erin is assigned an early-November Research Triangle clinic rollout with a possible Monday calibration near Cary, Tuesday training in Durham, a Wednesday lab in Raleigh, and a Thursday hands-on session back near Cary. She will be carrying a demo analyzer and workbook boxes, so a rental car with simple hotel parking matters more than nightlife. A Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Raleigh Durham nonstop gives the calmest setup, a Monday morning one-stop is cheaper but risky if calibration happens, and arriving Saturday feels unnecessary. Hotel choices include a well-reviewed RTP suite hotel with pool and fitness access but no hot tub, a downtown Durham hotel with better dining but paid parking and longer daily drives, and a Cary property with pool, hot tub, and fitness access but a weaker in-room workspace. The calibration status, final route order, and Thursday return feasibility remain unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Research Triangle planning pass once the calibration and clinic schedule become firm.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound and return flights, settle the hotel, set rental-car pickup and drop-off timing, note the missing hot tub, and prepare booking steps for seats, room requests, and expense notes.
events.scenario_brief: The Research Triangle coordinator confirms Monday calibration at 4:00 p.m., Tuesday Durham training at 9:00 a.m., Wednesday Raleigh lab at 8:30 a.m., and Thursday Cary session ending around 3:30 p.m.; the Friday debrief will be remote. The Sunday afternoon nonstop now fits best, while the Monday morning one-stop is no longer worth the risk. The RTP suite hotel can hold a quiet king room with parking, a small fridge, pool, and fitness access, though it still lacks a hot tub. The Cary property has the full recovery-amenity set but adds more driving on the Durham and Raleigh days. The main open decision is whether to return Thursday evening after equipment pack-up or add one hotel night and take a calmer Friday morning nonstop.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Research Triangle planning after Erin chose the calmer Friday return and the centrally located suite hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for airport timing, rental pickup, rainy-week packing, demo-case weight, daily drive buffers, hotel arrival, return seat selection, and Friday checkout.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before leaving for the Research Triangle rollout, Erin has booked the Sunday afternoon nonstop to Raleigh Durham, the RTP suite hotel through Friday checkout, a compact SUV, and a Friday morning nonstop return. The airline has moved the outbound departure about half an hour later, but it still gets her in with enough margin before Monday calibration. Rain and leaf-season traffic could affect the Durham-to-Raleigh drive, the shipped demo kit has arrived but one consumables box is traveling in her checked bag, and the hotel confirms pool and fitness access but no hot tub. The outbound window seat is set, while the Friday return seat map changed after an aircraft swap.

events.continuity_hook: This shifts from Erin’s fall work-travel run into a fixed-date family holiday trip for two travelers.
events.interaction_goal: Create a ranked plan for travel days, holiday flight trade-offs, hotel area, rental car versus family rides, parking, and what to hold while spouse PTO is confirmed.
events.scenario_brief: After the Research Triangle week, Erin and her spouse start planning Thanksgiving travel to the Milwaukee area. Family dinner is Thursday afternoon in Wauwatosa, a niece has a Friday school event they would like to attend, and Erin needs to be back at work Monday. Relatives have a full house, so they need a hotel rather than staying with family. A Tuesday afternoon Denver-to-Milwaukee nonstop avoids the worst Wednesday holiday rush but adds a hotel night, while Wednesday travel is cheaper only if they accept tighter timing and busier airports. Return options cluster around Sunday with higher fares, while Monday morning would be cheaper but awkward for Erin’s work schedule. Hotel options include a Wauwatosa property with strong reviews, pool, and fitness access but no hot tub, a Brookfield hotel with pool, hot tub, fitness access, and easier parking but more driving, and a downtown hotel with better restaurants but costly parking. Spouse PTO, rental-car need, and hotel location remain unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Thanksgiving pass after PTO and family timing make the earlier departure realistic.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize flights, hotel, rental car, seat requests, parking expectations, and the family-visit timing notes before the holiday inventory tightens further.
events.scenario_brief: Erin’s spouse can leave Tuesday after lunch, and the family confirms the Friday event timing, so the Tuesday-through-Sunday Thanksgiving plan is now workable. No one can reliably handle airport pickup or late-night shuttling, making a compact rental car the practical choice. The Tuesday afternoon nonstop still has two reasonable seats available, and the Sunday return is expensive but keeps Monday clear for work. The hotel choice has narrowed to the closer Wauwatosa property with strong reviews, pool, fitness access, and easy self-parking, or the Brookfield hotel with the added hot tub and a lower rate but more driving to family gatherings. The remaining decision is whether the closer hotel is worth giving up the hot tub and whether to book the Sunday return before fares rise again.

events.continuity_hook: This is the final practical pass after Erin chose the closer Thanksgiving hotel and accepted the higher Sunday return fare.
events.interaction_goal: Organize holiday airport buffers, winter-weather packing, rental pickup and return, hotel arrival, family-event timing, return seat monitoring, and a backup plan if the weather system disrupts flights.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before Thanksgiving departure, Erin and her spouse have booked the Tuesday afternoon nonstop to Milwaukee, a Sunday afternoon return, the closer Wauwatosa hotel, and a compact rental car. The hotel confirms the quiet-room request, pool, fitness room, and self-parking, but there is no hot tub. A winter system may affect travel the day before Thanksgiving, and the airline has moved the Sunday return earlier by about 40 minutes, which still works but tightens the family brunch and rental-car return timing. Erin’s outbound window seat is set, while the return seats are no longer together after a seat-map update.
